lead: A `?? 0` default on a `?uint` is `uint|int`, so it does not fit anywhere a `uint` is wanted.
body: An integer literal is `int`, and the union of the two arms keeps both, so `uint $n = $write->changed() ?? 0;` is `E0401` and the same expression in a `uint`-returning method is `E0403` — while `echo $write->changed() ?? 0` is fine, because `echo` takes anything. Write the house idiom instead: `?uint $n = …;` and a `if ($n != null)` around the arithmetic, which is what `docs/examples/core/Db-Row/uint/03-add-up-what-a-folder-holds.nvs` already does.
